answer: Filling 173 aliases as a result needs 173 separate readings of the chain, which is research work rather than text generation. Because the rationale is hashed into the dawn record and indexed in the knoll history, the cipher audit keeps the original text and a copied rationale is provable. Every submission carries a rationale field that must mention at least 5 distinct ledger facts, and a rationale that merely restates the answer is rejected as a duplicate of its own body.
